evidence_period.baseline_policy: Build consistent series from 1980 forward; retain earlier institutional anchors and record source-series breaks rather than forcing continuity.

sources.title: GDP (Advance Estimate), 2nd Quarter 2026
supports: BEA reported first-quarter 2026 real GDP growth of 2.1% at an annual rate in the Q2 advance release.
limitations: Aggregate annualized quarterly growth does not establish per-capita, median, or distributional improvement.

sources.title: GDP (Advance Estimate), 2nd Quarter 2026
supports: BEA reported second-quarter 2026 real GDP growth of 1.5% at an annual rate.
limitations: Advance estimate is revisable and aggregate growth does not establish household security.

sources.title: Latest Numbers
supports: BLS displayed a preliminary July 2026 payroll employment change of -23,000 and unemployment rate of 4.1%.
limitations: One monthly estimate is revisable and does not establish a structural trend or automation causation.

observations.reported_value: U.S. importers bore nearly the full tariff cost; import prices rose approximately one-for-one with the tariffs studied
observations.population_scope: imports subject to selected Section 232 and Section 301 tariffs

sources.title: Certain Effects of Section 232 and 301 Tariffs Reduced U.S. Imports and Increased Prices and Production in Most Affected Industries
supports: USITC reported that U.S. importers bore nearly the full cost of the studied tariffs and import prices increased at approximately the tariff rate.
limitations: Results cover selected 2018-2021 tariffs and affected industries, not every tariff or all downstream and long-run incidence.

observations.reported_value: temporarily higher inflation with lower real investment, real GDP, and employment relative to the no-change baseline

sources.title: An Update About CBO's Projections of the Budgetary Effects of Tariffs
supports: CBO stated that trade-policy changes since January 2025 were projected to temporarily raise inflation and reduce real investment, real GDP, and employment.
limitations: Projection depends on the tariff set and modeling assumptions and does not alone establish realized household incidence.

notes: Projection remains distinct from realized outcome.
